structs.name: GfxVertexBufferState
structs.size_evidence: not proven. IDA 72 (game-test 72) and builder 112 are priors only. No Replay code allocates, clears or copies this struct by its own size. Replay's only typed access is the pointer slot GfxCmdBufState.dynamicVertexBuffer at +0x11B0 (4528): R_InitCmdBufState@0x14198af30 stores `lea rax, s_cmdBufStateBlock` into it at 0x14198b08c (`mov [r14+11B0h], rax`).
unconfirmed: used (+0), total (+4), buffer (+8), wrappedBuffer (+16, 56 bytes): no Replay access to this struct's own fields found. Replay only reaches it through the GfxCmdBufState pointer, and the functions that touch that pointer's neighbours (R_InitCmdBufState, R_CmdBuf_BindZeroVertexBuffers32, R_InitComputeCmdBufState, R_SetupSceneCmdBufInput, R_TG_SetupTaskCmdBuf, R_SetCmdBufStatePointer) show no further reads of it
wrappedBuffer 56 vs builder 96 depends on GfxWrappedRWBuffer's Replay size, which is not measured here (game-test GfxWrappedRWBuffer is 56, IDA 96)
structs.notes: Pointed-to object is the global s_cmdBufStateBlock (0x150436310). R_CreateDynamicBuffers@0x1418da6e0 does memset_0(&s_cmdBufStateBlock, 0, 0xA8) at its start, but that 168-byte range also holds the separate globals s_dynBufSizeBytesB (+4), s_dynBufHandleB (+8), s_dynBufHandleC (+0x28) and s_dynBufAllocResultB (+0x78). So it is not one 72-byte (or 112-byte) object, and it cannot prove a size. The only xrefs to s_cmdBufStateBlock are in R_CreateDynamicBuffers and R_InitCmdBufState. Partial until a Replay function reads a member through the dynamicVertexBuffer pointer or a loader sizes the object.

structs.name: GfxCmdBuf
structs.size_evidence: no Replay proof of a 9120-byte object. Game-test users are all absent by name in Replay: RB_Async2D_InitContext, RB_Async2D_ShutdownContext, R_Async2D_Render, RB_Async2D_ExecCmdBuf, R_InitContext, R_InitCmdBuf, R_ShutdownCmdBuf (name search over functions found only R_CmdBuf_* and R_InitCmdBufState / R_InitComputeCmdBufState). No Replay name, type or typed global has the type GfxCmdBuf (types table search found none). Replay's per-draw command state is GfxCmdBufState (IDA 10368, base ComputeCmdBufState 4328), whose dynamicIndexBuffer (+0x11A8) and dynamicVertexBuffer (+0x11B0) are stored by R_InitCmdBufState.
unconfirmed: device, cmdBufIndex, cmdList, descState (9064), useImmediateContext, constantBufferAllocations: no Replay access found
structs.notes: Limit: a whole-binary search for a 2380h (9120) allocation constant was not run (scan_disasm over the full text range exceeds the tool budget). Absence rests on the name, type and xref checks above. The embedding parents GfxDrawCallOutput (9136) and GfxAsync2DFrameData (22784) are also absent from Replay type data (see those entries). Coordinator: if you want stronger proof, run a sized-allocation search for 9120 with the existing allocator names.

structs.name: GfxAsync2DFrameData
structs.size_evidence: no Replay proof of a 22784-byte object. No Replay function has Async2D in its name (functions table: 0 rows for '%Async%2D%' or '%Async2D%'; the R_*/RB_* names containing 2D are RB_InitFilterParams2D, R_Triangle2D_ComputePointWeights, R_Image_CreateDefault2DTexture, R_TG_AddScriptViewTask2D, which were not decompiled and are not evidence either way). No Replay string contains Async2D, async 2d or PPFX (strings table, 0 rows). No typed address in the types table has this type (0 rows for GfxAsync2DFrameData, GfxCmdBuf, GfxVertexBufferState, GfxDrawCallOutput declarations).
structs.notes: Absent: no allocation, no global of this type, no by-value use in a Replay-typed struct, no function that takes or returns it. What Replay uses instead: GfxCmdBufState (IDA 10368) for command state, R_CreateDynamicBuffers@0x1418da6e0 for the dynamic upload and wrapped buffers (168-byte pool blocks with a 104-byte handle stride, 'mayhemChannelsVbPool' and 'mayhemChannelsBufferPool' labels). Those pool blocks are not GfxAsync2DFrameData. The absence of a global is limited the same way as for GfxCmdBuf: no exhaustive sized-allocation search was run, only the typed-address and name checks.
